title.en: History: Freedom Struggle in Tamil Nadu

text.en: Raju heard Tamil patriots sung about in a song. "Who fought for freedom in Tamil Nadu?" he asked.

Tamil Nadu played a big part in the freedom struggle. V. O. Chidambaram Pillai started the Swadeshi Steam Navigation Company at Thoothukudi to challenge British shipping. Subramania Bharati inspired people with patriotic songs.
Subramania Siva, Vanchinathan, who killed the collector Ashe, and Vanchi Aiyar were revolutionaries. S. Satyamurti and Rajaji led the Congress, and the Vedaranyam Salt March of 1930 led by Rajaji was held in the Cauvery delta.
Women like Dr Muthulakshmi Reddy, Rukmini Lakshmipathi, Ambujammal and Vedaratnam took part, and Tiruppur Kumaran gave his life with the national flag. Kamaraj, a leader of the Congress, later became a great Chief Minister.

board.text: Tamil Nadu's vibrant role in freedom struggle

text.en: Early political voice began with Madras Native Association (1852) led by Gazulu Lakshminarasu Chetty, and the Madras Mahajana Sabha (1884) with P. Rangaiah Naidu.
Journalists G. Subramania Iyer started The Hindu (1878) and Swadesamitran (Tamil daily, 1899) to spread political awareness into villages.

After Bengal's 1905 partition, Tirunelveli district blazed with Swadeshi spirit! 'Kappalottiya Thamizhan' V. O. Chidambaram Pillai launched two Swadeshi ships—SS Gallia and SS Lavo—at Thoothukudi in 1906.
When British magistrates jailed V.O.C. and Subramania Siva for sedition—forcing V.O.C. to pull an oil press in Coimbatore jail—Tirunelveli erupted in India's first political industrial strike.

board.text: 1908 Coral Mill strike & V.O.C.'s jail sacrifice

text.en: Poet-patriot Mahakavi Subramania Bharati poured fire into 'Vande Mataram', 'Achamillai Achamillai' and India weekly from Pondicherry.

board.text: Subramania Bharati's fearless songs of freedom

text.en: Alongside peaceful boycotts, revolutionaries built Bharata Matha Association; V. V. S. Aiyar trained youth at Pondicherry and Vanchinathan shot Collector Ashe at Maniyachi junction in 1911.
In 1916, Dr Annie Besant launched the Home Rule League at Adyar alongside New India paper and George Joseph's labour advocacy in Madurai.

board.text: 1916: Annie Besant's Home Rule from Adyar

text.en: During Non-Cooperation (1920), C. Rajagopalachari (Rajaji), S. Satyamurti and E. V. Ramasamy (Periyar) led Khadi sales, temperance pickets and court boycotts; Periyar even led the 1924 Vaikom Satyagraha.
In 1927, Congressmen in Madras pulled down the hated Statue of Colonel Neill (infamous for 1857 cruelties), led by fearless volunteers like S. N. Somayajulu.
When Gandhi marched to Dandi in 1930, Rajaji led 99 satyagrahis from Tiruchirappalli to coastal Vedaranyam, bravely breaking the salt law on 30 April 1930!
Remember Rukmini Lakshmipathi—the first woman arrested in the Vedaranyam salt satyagraha—plus brave T. Prakasam in Madras during Simon protests.
In Tiruppur on 11 January 1932, police lathi-charged protesters; dying with the national flag gripped upright in his hand, 'Kodi Kaatha Kumaran' (Tiruppur Kumaran) became immortal.
Look at selfless women leaders too: Anjalai Ammal of Cuddalore (called 'South India's Jhansi Rani' by Gandhi), Ambujammal, Padmasani Ammal and Dr Muthulakshmi Reddy.
In 1937, Rajaji formed the Congress government in Madras Presidency, passing temple-entry laws and peasant debt relief before resigning in 1939 over WWII.

board.text: 1937 Congress ministry & 1942 Quit India in TN

text.en: During 1942 Quit India, Tamil Nadu roared with K. Kamaraj's grass-roots mobilisation, students strikes, and K. T. Bhashyam and S. S. Viswanathan.

board.text: Kamaraj anchors 1942 Quit India across districts

text.en: Even abroad, Tamil youth joined Subhas Chandra Bose's INA, helping fund and fight alongside Netaji.

board.text: Tamil youth in Netaji's Azad Hind Fauj

text.en: Remember hero titles cleanly: V.O.C. = Kappalottiya Thamizhan; Kumaran = Kodi Kaatha Kumaran; Bharati = Mahakavi; Satyamurti = silver-tongued mentor to Kamaraj.
Notice the twin tracks in Tamil Nadu: Swadeshi ships/poems/boycotts plus social-reform conscience ensuring freedom lifted every citizen.
After 1947, veteran patriot K. Kamaraj transformed Tamil Nadu through free midday meals and thousands of rural schools.

board.text: From freedom fighters to builders of Tamil Nadu

text.en: To connect the story: 1884 Mahajana Sabha -> 1906 V.O.C. & Bharati -> 1930 Vedaranyam & 1932 Kumaran -> 1942 Kamaraj & Victory.
Knowing how ordinary weavers, students, women and poets in Tamil Nadu fought keeps our democratic heritage alive.
